title: Non-blocking findings from PR #327's review (frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings)
description: Tracked follow-ups for non-blocking findings raised in pr-reviewer's review of PR #327 (frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings) -- one found during the review's own manual browser walkthrough, one corroborated (plus one additional) by the code-review skill run in the background during that same review -- so neither is lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: TradingModeSettingsForm's client-side validation errors (the `errors` state in `TradingModeFields`, frontend/src/features/settings/components/TradingModeSettingsForm.tsx) are only recomputed inside `handleSubmit`, never cleared or re-validated as the user edits a field or toggles the mode radio. Reproduced live: (1) switch to Day Trader mode, type an invalid long-term leg (e.g. 'abc'), click Save -- the format error appears correctly; (2) without clicking Save again, correct the field to a valid value (e.g. '25m') -- the red error border and 'Must be a positive whole number...' helper text remain displayed even though the current field value is now valid, until the user clicks Save again (which re-validates and clears it). The same gap applies to `handleModeChange`: toggling Swing -> Day Trader re-shows the triple fields with whatever stale `errors` were set on the previous attempt, before any new edit or submit. Momentary/cosmetic (the final submitted data is always correctly validated), but misleading mid-edit. Fix: clear (or re-validate) the affected leg's entry in `errors` inside `handleTripleChange`/`handleModeChange` as the user edits, not only inside `handleSubmit`.

`useUpdateTradingMode`'s `onSuccess` calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries()` with no filter (frontend/src/features/settings/hooks/useUpdateTradingMode.ts), refetching every mounted query app-wide on every trading-mode save, not just the documented trading-mode-dependent set (stocks/watchlist/portfolio queries). This is a deliberate, already-justified tradeoff (see the parent task's own `decisions` entry and this PR's review notes) rather than an oversight, and isn't blocking -- but worth reconsidering later if this ever causes a noticeable request burst in practice (e.g. once the settings feature or another feature's `queryKeys.ts` registry makes an explicit, maintainable invalidation list cheaper to keep in sync than it is today).

decisions.decision: Fixed the stale-validation-error bug by clearing the edited leg's entry from `errors` inside `handleTripleChange` (delete just that key) and clearing the whole `errors` object inside `handleModeChange`, rather than fully re-validating (recomputing pass/fail) on every keystroke.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item explicitly allows either 'clear (or re-validate)'. A clear-only fix satisfies the reported bug (a corrected value's stale red error/helper text no longer lingers past the edit) without introducing a second behavior change: full live re-validation would also start showing a new error the instant a field goes empty or briefly invalid mid-edit (e.g. typing '2' then '25' then '25m' would flash 'Must be a positive whole number...' after the first two keystrokes), which is more intrusive UX than this bug report asked for and wasn't reproduced/requested as a separate problem. `handleSubmit` already re-validates everything from scratch before calling `mutate()`, so clearing (rather than re-validating) never risks submitting unvalidated data -- only the previous validation pass's cached error is discarded early. Rejected alternative: re-validate the single edited leg's own format on every keystroke (`setErrors(current => ({ ...current, [leg]: validateLeg(...) }))`) -- would also fix the reported bug, but was judged to add exactly the naggy-live-validation downside above for no reporting-required benefit; if a future task wants live inline validation as its own explicit feature, it can build on this clear-first baseline without conflicting with it.

decisions.decision: Implemented a scoped version of the trading-mode invalidation: `useUpdateTradingMode`'s `onSuccess` now calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ... })` three times, once per `stocksKeys.all`/`watchlistKeys.all`/`portfolioKeys.all` (a new `all: ['stocks'] as const` was added to `features/stocks/hooks/queryKeys.ts` for this, mirroring the `all` convention `watchlistKeys`/`portfolioKeys` already had), instead of the previous unfiltered `queryClient.invalidateQueries()`. This does not amend the parent task's own already-recorded `decisions` entry (which stays as an accurate record of what was decided and why at that time) -- it supersedes that call for this codebase going forward via this task's own fresh entry.
decisions.rationale: Re-weighed the parent decision's own stated objection (cross-feature import coupling, and silent under-invalidation if a future mode-aware endpoint isn't added to the list) against the actual current codebase state: every other feature's mutation hook (useAddPosition, useAddWatchlistItem, useDeletePosition, useRecordFollowUpReview) already imports its own feature's `queryKeys.ts` and invalidates via its `xKeys.all` prefix constant -- importing three such constants into one settings-feature hook is the same established mechanism used three times, not a new one, and each `xKeys.all` is deliberately documented as a public, shared prefix (each file's own header comment already calls itself 'Shared TanStack Query key conventions'). The 'silently under-invalidate a future mode-aware endpoint' risk is also more contained than the parent decision characterized it: docs/architecture/API.md's own definition of which endpoints depend on trading mode already enumerates only `stocks`/`watchlist`/`portfolio` routes, and any *new* endpoint added under one of those three existing feature namespaces is automatically covered for free by TanStack Query's prefix-matching invalidation (the same 'impossible by construction' argument `portfolioKeys.ts`'s own `risk`/`closedTrades` nesting already relies on) -- the residual risk is narrowed to a hypothetical brand-new *fourth* top-level feature area becoming mode-dependent, which would already require updating API.md's own documented list at the same time, a natural point to also update this invalidation call. Weighed against that narrowed risk: the previous blanket invalidation refetches every mounted query on every mode save, including features API.md never documents as mode-dependent (scanner params, IBKR connection status, daily-homework/trade-journal data) -- a real, avoidable cost on a page whose own settings save is otherwise cheap. Verified via a new unit test (`invalidates only the stocks/watchlist/portfolio query-key prefixes...`, TradingModeSettingsForm.test.tsx) spying on `queryClient.invalidateQueries` directly, asserting exactly the three scoped calls and never an unfiltered one. Rejected alternative: keep the blanket call and only add a decision confirming it (the checklist's other allowed outcome) -- rejected because, on reflection, the coupling cost this task's checklist raised for reconsideration is already paid elsewhere in this codebase for single-feature invalidations, so paying it once more for three already-existing, already-public constants was judged worth the reduced unrelated-refetch cost; also rejected keeping the exact same behavior via three inline literal arrays (`['stocks']`/['watchlist']`/['portfolio']`) instead of importing the constants, since that would silently drift from each feature's own key definition if a feature ever renamed its top-level segment, whereas importing the shared constant can't drift by construction.

decisions.decision: Fixed pr-reviewer's blocking finding on PR #328 (needs_work) by adding `settingsKeys.tradingMode` as a fourth scoped `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ... })` call inside `useUpdateTradingMode`'s `onSuccess`, alongside the existing `stocksKeys.all`/`watchlistKeys.all`/`portfolioKeys.all` three. Chose invalidating the query (over the review comment's other suggested option, `setQueryData`-ing the mutation response directly into the `settingsKeys.tradingMode` cache slot) because it's the same mechanism already used for the other three keys -- one consistent pattern in this `onSuccess` handler rather than two different cache-update strategies side by side -- and because `TradingModeFields` never re-reads the query's cached data after its own mount anyway (it seeds its `useState` once from `initialData`), so there's no in-place-update UX win from `setQueryData` here that invalidation doesn't already give the *next* mount.
decisions.rationale: Verified this genuinely fixes the reported bug and that the new test genuinely would have caught it, by mutation-testing it: temporarily removed the `settingsKeys.tradingMode` invalidation line again and reran `TradingModeSettingsForm.test.tsx` -- both the updated 'invalidates only the stocks/watchlist/portfolio/settings query-key prefixes' test (now asserting 4 calls including `['settings', 'trading-mode']`) and the new 'keeps the settings query itself in sync...' test failed (2 failed / 13 passed), the latter timing out on `queryClient.getQueryData(settingsKeys.tradingMode)?.mode` never becoming `'day_trader'` -- exactly the reviewer's reproduced symptom (the settings cache never reflecting the just-saved mode). Restored the fix and reran: 15/15 passing. The new test intentionally does NOT just assert `invalidateQueries` call args/count (which is what the pre-existing 3 tests already did and none of them caught this regression, per the review) -- it (1) asserts the actual cache content (`queryClient.getQueryData(settingsKeys.tradingMode)`) reflects the newly-persisted mode after the mutation succeeds, and (2) unmounts and re-mounts a fresh `TradingModeSettingsForm` instance against the same `QueryClient` (simulating the client-side navigate-away-and-back the review reproduced with Playwright) with the client's `staleTime` set to main.tsx's real 60s (rather than a fresh test `QueryClient`'s implicit `staleTime: 0`, which would refetch on every mount regardless of invalidation and mask this exact bug) to confirm the freshly-mounted form shows the saved mode/triple rather than the stale pre-save cache. Rejected alternative: assert `queryClient.getQueryState(settingsKeys.tradingMode)?.isInvalidated === true` synchronously right after the mutation resolves (the review comment's other suggested check) -- rejected as more timing-fragile in practice, since `isInvalidated` flips back to `false` as soon as the background refetch TanStack Query auto-triggers for an active query completes, which can race with when a `waitFor` callback happens to poll; asserting the eventual cache *content* and the real remount behavior avoids that race and tests the user-facing symptom directly instead of an internal flag.

comments.summary: Re-review after the prior needs_work: the fix adds `settingsKeys.tradingMode` as a fourth scoped `invalidateQueries` call in `useUpdateTradingMode`'s `onSuccess`, alongside the pre-existing `stocksKeys.all`/`watchlistKeys.all`/`portfolioKeys.all` three -- confirmed still exactly 4 explicit, scoped keys, not a reintroduction of the original PR #327 blanket `queryClient.invalidateQueries()` (no-arg call). Re-ran the exact live-browser regression scenario myself with a fresh Playwright script against a freshly-started `make backend`/`make frontend` (no MCP browser tool available in this session, same as the prior review round): saved a Day Trader mode switch with a distinctive triple (30m/6m/1m), clicked the Dashboard nav link (real SPA route change), then the Settings nav link back, all within the 60s staleTime window. The form now shows the just-saved mode/triple correctly on remount (previously it showed the stale pre-save data) -- no console errors, no failed network requests.

Independently mutation-tested the new regression test (not just trusted the task-worker's own mutation-testing claim in its decisions entry): temporarily removed the `settingsKeys.tradingMode` invalidateQueries call, reran `TradingModeSettingsForm.test.tsx` -- 2 of 15 tests failed as expected (the 4-call invalidation-scope assertion and the new 'keeps the settings query itself in sync...' remount test, the latter timing out waiting for the cache to reflect the saved mode). Restored the fix from git and confirmed `git diff`/`git status` were clean afterward (all 15 tests passing again) before proceeding with the rest of the review.

Minor bookkeeping fix made as part of accepting this task: checklist item 2 (the blanket-invalidation reconsideration) was left `done: false` even though decisions entry 2 documents that this PR actually implemented the scoped invalidation it was flagging for reconsideration, superseding the parent task's blanket-invalidation decision. Corrected to `done: true` in this same review pass since the item's own concern is resolved by this PR's change -- not filed as a separate follow-up task since it's a same-task bookkeeping correction being made at the moment this task closes, not a new finding about the code.

review.notes: Re-review of PR #328 after the prior needs_work verdict (settingsKeys.tradingMode dropped from the scoped invalidation). Verified the fix directly: frontend/src/features/settings/hooks/useUpdateTradingMode.ts now invalidates exactly 4 scoped keys (stocksKeys.all, watchlistKeys.all, portfolioKeys.all, settingsKeys.tradingMode) -- confirmed via git diff this round introduced no change back toward the original PR #327 blanket invalidateQueries(). Re-ran backend pytest --cov=app: 1406 passed, 100% coverage (no backend files touched, unchanged baseline). Frontend yarn vitest run --coverage: 906/906 passing (up from 905, the 1 new remount-regression test), 99.78%/99.1%/99.8%/99.83% stmt/branch/fn/line -- above the 90% gate. Backend ruff+mypy clean; frontend eslint+tsc clean; scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py clean; scripts/validate_tasks.py clean (319 files, no violations). code-review skill (background, full diff of PR #328) returned zero findings -- independently confirmed the fix matches docs/architecture/API.md's documented trading-mode-dependent endpoint set and that no other consumer of settingsKeys.tradingMode/stocksKeys.all exists that this change could break. Did my own live browser walkthrough (see comment above) reproducing the exact prior regression scenario end to end and confirmed it's fixed, plus independently mutation-tested the new regression test by removing the fix and confirming it fails (see comment above) rather than trusting the task-worker's own mutation-testing claim. Ran `make e2e`: 26/26 specs passing (dashboard/navigation/portfolio/scanner/stock-analysis/watchlist), no regression. No backend files touched, so backend/openapi.json correctly untouched. No new components added, so no common/-vs-feature-specific placement question applies. Both checklist items now have decisions entries with genuine rationale and are marked done (item 2's done flag corrected this round, see comment above). No new non-blocking findings this round beyond the checklist bookkeeping fix already applied directly -- no new follow-up task filed. Posting this verdict as a `gh pr review --comment` (COMMENTED), never --approve/--request-changes; not merging -- that's pr-decision + pr-merger's job.
